context.why: Stories 1 and 2 are accepted: the API reads complete records and writes them on the real routes. The registry's SerializerFactory (fairdm/registry/factories.py) is the one builder, building each registered type's serializer from the base's common_fields plus the type's resolved field list, and generate_viewset (fairdm/api/viewsets.py) uses config.get_serializer_class() and checks a named serializer_class against the sample or measurement base. This story is for the portal developer: registering a type is enough to get a working API for it, the registration decides what it carries, a mistake is reported when the portal starts and not when a caller meets it, and the router can be extended. Much of this may already behave correctly; prove each task with a test, and where a test passes on first run confirm it can fail by breaking the code it covers. T033 is already met and is not yours.
spec_sections: Edge Cases (a type's plural name changes)
plan_sections: D3. Viewsets (the base check in generate_viewset)
prior_decisions: decisions.md D9 and D16: the check that a developer's serializer builds on BaseSampleSerializer or BaseMeasurementSerializer lives in generate_viewset and must apply to whatever config.get_serializer_class() returns, including a configuration that OVERRIDES get_serializer_class (which bypasses both the named serializer_class and the factory). The base carries the parent narrowing, the creator credit and the manage-level rules, so a serializer off the base would let any signed-in person write. T029 adds that case in tests/test_api/test_viewsets.py.

plan D4: one Django system check in a new fairdm/api/checks.py, registered from the API app's ready() (fairdm/api/apps.py). For each registered sample and measurement type it compares the model's required fields (no default, not blank, not null, editable, not auto-created) with the writable fields of the type's API serializer and returns a django.core.checks.Error naming the type and the field for each one missing. Look at fairdm/conf/checks.py for how this project writes and numbers checks and follow it. Tests call the check function directly with a type registered for the test (see tests/registry_models and tests/test_registry/conftest.py for how tests register types) and assert on the error's id and that it names the type and field, not on its wording.

plan D4: fairdm/api/router.py wraps registration of sample and measurement types in two try/except blocks that log a warning and carry on. Remove them so a type whose endpoints cannot be built stops the portal with the real error. T031 proves it by building the registration for a broken configuration; refactor the module-level loops into a function the test can call if needed, keeping `fairdm_api_router` as the public name.

Carried from story 1: a type registered with NO field list falls back to FieldInspector's defaults (fairdm/utils/inspection.py), which include `options`, an internal JSON field, and `tags`, which the API returned as null whatever the record holds. The API's default for such a type must leave both out. Do this in how the serializer's field list is resolved for the API, without changing what the forms, tables or filters get from the same defaults.

Carried from story 1: a filter a registered type declares on one of its own relations is generated as a ModelChoiceFilter matching database numbers. FR-005 says no request the API accepts may contain a database number. Story 1 already gives the API its own copy of a type's filter set with `dataset` and `sample` matching uuid (see how in fairdm/api/, decisions.md D17). Extend that so every relation filter the API serves for a record type or contributor matches on uuid where the related model has one, and a relation whose model has no uuid is left out of the API's copy. The portal's pages keep their filter sets unchanged. Put its test with T028's class or a sibling class in tests/test_api/test_viewsets.py.

FR-027 and decisions.md D11: a generated route is `samples/<plural-name>/` or `measurements/<plural-name>/` with route names `samples-<slug>-list` and so on. T032 proves a sample type and a measurement type with the same plural name get different route names.

T034: a viewset registered on fairdm_api_router (fairdm/api/router.py) is served and appears in the schema at /api/v1/schema/. Register it inside the test and undo the registration afterwards so no other test sees it (the router and URL caches are module state: clear what you touch).
T027 goes in tests/test_registry/test_factories.py as a new class TestSerializerFactory beside the existing factory test classes.
No architecture decision record is needed for this story.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a registered type with no API configuration, with serializer_fields, and with only fields, when its serializer is built, then it carries the common fields plus respectively the defaults (without options and tags), the API list, and the general list, and builds on the base for its kind.
Given a registration naming a serializer_class and one overriding get_serializer_class, when the route is built, then its serializer is the one the configuration returns.
Given a configuration overriding get_serializer_class with a serializer off the base, when its endpoints are built, then ImproperlyConfigured is raised.
Given a registered type whose API fields omit a required model field, when the system check runs, then it returns an error naming the type and field, and a complete registration returns none.
Given a type whose endpoints cannot be built, when the router registration runs, then the error propagates.
Given generated routes, then addresses come from the plural name under samples/ or measurements/ and same-named sample and measurement types get different route names.
Given a viewset a developer registers on the router, then it is served and is in the schema.
Given the failing tests from T027 to T034, when the implementation lands, then they pass.

Given docs/portal-development/restful-api.md and the registry pages that mention serializers (grep docs/ for serializer_fields, serializer_class and get_serializer_class), when read against the branch, then they describe the options, the base serializers, the start-up check, addresses and renaming, the filters by identifier, and the router.
